metadata.title: DIY Garage Door Windows
metadata.description:
Join Vicki & Steph from Mother Daughter Projects as they add a decorative and heat-reducing DIY to Steph's garage door windows. (show more)

Products Used (Affiliate)
Painter's tape - http://amzn.to/2noN5Yt
Frosted Glass Spray - http://amzn.to/2malxVY 

For more details visit: http://www.motherdaughterprojects.com/blog/garage-door-diy-windows

FYI: We are not professionals, and we don’t claim to be. This is what we found worked for our project. Yours may need a little different approach. Safety first!

nodes.plm_action: Applying blue painter's tape to windows
nodes.plm_caption:
A video of two women transforming a garage door. They start by cleaning off all of the windows and then taping off the windows, then they sand the windows, spray paint the inside and outside of the window, and finally, they put windows on. At the end, they have transformed a garage door and house. The video is a tutorial.
The garage door has many windows on it. It's a very long door. There is blue tape on the windows and the frame of the windows. The windows are closed off and taped off.
At the end, there are two arrows on the garage door.
The garage door is closed at the beginning and the end. There is no door on it. There is a white garage door on the house after the women transform it. There are trees behind the garage door and house.

summary.brief: The two presenters frost‑spray the garage‑door windows and reveal the finished look.
summary.detailed: After removing the original window inserts, the women tape a cross‑shaped mask onto each garage‑door window and cover the surrounding area with scrap paper. Wearing face masks, they spray two coats of Rust‑Oleum frosted‑glass spray onto the taped windows from inside the garage. They then open the garage door and run a fan to vent the fumes, let the coating dry, and finally remove the paper and tape, exposing a subtle frosted pattern that reduces light and heat. They comment on the noticeable difference and express satisfaction with the decorative result before ending the tutorial.

action.detailed: Create cross‑shaped tape masks on each window, cover the door with scrap paper, spray two coats of frosted‑glass spray while wearing a mask, vent the garage with the door open and a fan, let the coating dry, then remove the tape and paper to reveal the frosted finish.
action.actor: the two women presenting the tutorial

summary.brief: Mother and daughter frost the garage‑door windows with a cross‑tape pattern.
summary.detailed: After removing the original window inserts, Vicki and Steph create a cross‑shaped template on the first garage‑door window and copy the same pattern to the other windows using blue painter’s tape. While the first coat dries they open the garage door and run a fan to vent fumes. After the second coat dries they peel off the paper and tape, revealing a subtle frosted finish that reduces glare and heat, and they smile at the improved, decorative look.
